note: Honest coverage frontier for the operator console. status: present = a runnable oracle drives real code and asserts THIS scenario's behaviour; pending = declared, reviewable debt — specified behaviour with no oracle (and in several rows here, no implementation); retrospective_gap = shipped without a driving test (must be zero for governed UI). THE ORACLES MOVED. The React frontend/ these rows used to name was deleted on 2026-07-30 under ADR-0015 (4b0e9763), taking contract.test.ts / sse.test.ts / controls.test.tsx and the rest with it; the 18 rows went on reading as executing coverage and executed nothing until TG-259 re-pointed them. What certifies the console today is (a) the Playwright suite in deploy/console/v2/e2e, run by its run.sh against the SERVED index.html — note that deploy/console/v2/e2e/postdeploy is deliberately outside that glob because it needs a live credential, so an oracle there is NOT executing coverage; (b) Go tests under core/ for the server half of an API-contract scenario; and (c) deploy/served_console_test.go, which binds what is served to what is certified (REQ-617). Where the served console simply does not implement the specified behaviour — the OpenAPI-generated client layer, SSE reconnect, manifest replay, a LedgerVerifier verdict on screen, a policy-API kill-switch write, a users/roles/on-call admin panel — the row says pending and says why. A mapping that named a file which merely exists would recreate the exact defect TG-259 fixed.

scenarios.name: The console builds its API layer only from the generated OpenAPI client
scenarios.test: NO ORACLE, AND NO IMPLEMENTATION. The React frontend/ this scenario is written about was removed under ADR-0015. The served console builds its requests with hand-written fetch calls against /api/v1/**; nothing is generated from the OpenAPI document. The gencontracts gate proves the SERVER's registered routes match the published contract — it says nothing about how the console constructs a request, so pointing this row at it would claim coverage the tree does not have.
scenarios.note: Searched the Playwright console suite (deploy/console/v2/e2e/, ~65 oracles run by run.sh, which derives its list from the directory so nothing can be added and silently skipped) on 2026-08-07 and did NOT find a driving oracle. Nothing in the suite touches the generated-OpenAPI-client constraint (REQ-601), manifest replay (REQ-607), or the admin panel (REQ-612). These are pending ORACLES against built features (spec/010 is 9/9 on tasks), not pending work.

scenarios.name: A dropped SSE stream shows a disconnected indicator and reconnects

scenarios.test: deploy/console/v2/e2e/keyboard-operability.mjs drives the real renderer and asserts roles, names, states AND activation ('every run row is an option carrying selection state'; 'the run list is exactly ONE tab stop (roving tabindex)'; 'ENTER selects a run (attributes alone are not operability)'; 'SPACE toggles a stage disclosure'). deploy/console/v2/e2e/aria-state.mjs asserts published state across the console — 'every nav item: painted-active <=> aria-current=page', 'every facet chip: painted-on <=> aria-pressed', 'palette input is a combobox', 'ArrowDown moves aria-selected AND aria-activedescendant with it'. deploy/console/v2/e2e/contrast-tokens.mjs asserts WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1) over the whole token table in BOTH themes. HONEST LIMIT: the 'visible focus indicator' clause is not asserted as an indicator; deploy/console/v2/e2e/palette-focus.mjs asserts focus RESTORATION, not visibility.

scenarios.name: The console never enforces a safety decision client-side

scenarios.name: When mutation is enabled an authorized operator gains operational controls
scenarios.test: deploy/console/v2/e2e/candidates-ratify.mjs drives BOTH directions of the server's authorization answer: with caller_can_act=true the oracle clicks the ratify verb and waits for the write to land ('ratify: exactly one write must be issued'), which a disabled control could not produce; with caller_can_act=false, 'read-only: both verbs must still be RENDERED, not hidden' and 'read-only: every verb must be DISABLED when caller_can_act=false', plus 'read-only: the form fields must be disabled too'. deploy/console/v2/e2e/manifest-review.mjs asserts the same pair on the manifest verbs ('controls: a review surface must offer its verbs' / 'read-only: every control must be DISABLED when the server says caller_can_act=false'). HONEST LIMIT: the driven precondition is the API's per-caller authorization (caller_can_act), not the may_actuate posture.

scenarios.name: An approver action is gated by role and re-checked server-side
scenarios.test: temporal/runner/vote_admission_test.go is the server-side re-check (REQ-1516, the live frozen-at-gate mechanism — the former core/policy MayApprove drills retired with that lane under TG-488 B26/TG-463): TestAVoteFromOutsideApproveByNeverReleasesTheAction asserts a non-member's vote never releases the action, TestVoterAdmittedIsFailClosed asserts the empty-set/empty-voter directions fail CLOSED rather than open, and TestAVoteFromInsideApproveByStillApproves keeps the member path honest. core/httpapi/decisions_test.go — TestDecisionsHandler — asserts the authority is computed from the principal on the server ('an operator session must be able to act on a pending decision'; 'a machine principal must NOT be authorized to act'), never taken from the client. deploy/console/v2/e2e/approvals-reachable.mjs is the console half: it treats that server answer as final.

scenarios.name: A non-approver cannot act on a pending decision
scenarios.test: deploy/console/v2/e2e/approvals-reachable.mjs drives a decisions payload with caller_can_act=false and asserts 'rows still render when the operator lacks authority', 'but NO vote control is offered without caller_can_act' (zero Approve, zero Deny), and 'and it says why, rather than showing a dead button'. The oracle counts rows against the payload rather than checking for the mere existence of a button, so it cannot pass vacuously on an empty queue.
